batch_node.name: duo page v0.2.0
batch_node.description: The /duo page (req-duo-page): one page, the account-map graph panel with its projection, elevation, layout (account-map.js) and seven scene searches; the posture strip (the plugin's own panel type, req-duo-panel-posture); seven standard tables, each over a search this bundle owns. Every search is scoped by the page's ?account= (the account's name; empty = every account). References no entity outside this file and no instance data: the page renders whatever Duo nodes the grid holds. v0.2.0: the map's graph panel routes a click on an Okta org (a system that requests a second factor) to /okta for that org, through the panel's nav_rules.

node.name: Duo
node.description: The operator's front page for a Duo account in a FedRAMP 20x environment: the account map at the top, then the posture strip, the protected applications and the policy each enforces, the policies, the users not doing MFA, outstanding bypass codes, administrators and device health. ?account=<account name> selects an account; without it the page shows every account, which is the one account on a grid that holds one.

node.name: Duo account map
node.description: The account at the centre; its protected applications on the left with whatever sends users to them (an Okta org, a VPN) further out; the policies they enforce on the right; the groups they admit below; the enrolled-device types above, one tile per kind with its count. Lines are policy enforcement (application → policy) and group access (application → group); tenancy is the layout itself. An application with no line to a policy runs under the Global Policy. Click an Okta org to open its /okta page.

node.name: Duo posture
node.description: The front of the account in one strip: MFA coverage (bypass, lockout, enrollment), the factor mix from phishable to phishing-resistant, access (applications, Admin API grants, new-user policy), administration, and device trust. Every count that rests on a field no collector has observed says so instead of reading as zero.

node.name: Protected applications
node.description: Every application in the account: what it is, who may use it, and — for an Admin API application — what it may do to Duo itself. The policy each enforces is the next table.

columns.title: Application
columns.header_tooltip: The application's name in Duo.

columns.title: Type
columns.header_tooltip: Duo's integration type: okta (Duo as Okta's authenticator), sso-generic / sso-oidc-generic (Duo SSO), adminapi, authapi, websdk, rdp, unix, radius, ldapproxy, …

columns.title: User access
columns.header_tooltip: ALL_USERS, NO_USERS, or PERMITTED_GROUPS (only the groups the application admits). A dash means not observed.

columns.title: Admin API grants

columns.title: Self-service

columns.title: Integration key
columns.header_tooltip: Duo's DI… id. Blank until a collector observes it.

node.name: Policy by application
node.description: Which custom policy each application enforces, for everyone (app) or for certain groups (group policy, in stack order). An application missing here enforces nothing of its own: it runs under the Global Policy, shown in the policies table.

columns.title: Application
columns.header_tooltip: The protected application.

columns.title: Type
columns.header_tooltip: Duo's integration type.

columns.title: Policy
columns.header_tooltip: The custom policy the application enforces.

columns.title: Applies to
columns.header_tooltip: app: every user of the application. group_app: only members of the listed groups — a group policy.

columns.title: Groups
columns.header_tooltip: For a group policy: the groups it targets in this application.

columns.title: Stack
columns.header_tooltip: For a group policy: its position in the application's group-policy stack; order decides which applies to a user in several groups.

columns.title: New users
columns.header_tooltip: The policy's New User Policy: enroll, deny, or no-mfa (unenrolled users get in without MFA). A dash means the section is inherited or not observed.

node.name: Policies
node.description: The Global Policy and every custom policy: what an unenrolled user may do and which authentication methods are allowed. A dash is a section the policy does not set (it inherits) or that no collector has observed — never a permissive default.

columns.title: Policy
columns.header_tooltip: The policy's name.

columns.title: Global
columns.header_tooltip: ✓ for the Global Policy, which every application inherits section by section unless overridden.

columns.title: New users
columns.header_tooltip: enroll, deny, or no-mfa. no-mfa lets an unenrolled user in without a second factor.

columns.title: Allowed methods
columns.header_tooltip: The Authentication Methods allowed list. sms and phonecall are phishable; webauthn-roaming / webauthn-platform are phishing-resistant; smart-card exists only on Duo Federal.

columns.title: Policy key
columns.header_tooltip: Duo's PO… id. Blank until observed.

node.name: Users not doing MFA — or not known to
node.description: Users in bypass (MFA skipped), locked out, or disabled; users with no enrolled authenticator; and users whose enrollment no collector has observed — the third state, listed rather than assumed enrolled.

columns.title: User
columns.header_tooltip: The Duo username.

columns.title: Name
columns.header_tooltip: Full name as Duo holds it.

columns.title: Status
columns.header_tooltip: active, bypass (skips MFA), locked out, disabled, pending deletion.

columns.title: Enrolled
columns.header_tooltip: ✓ has at least one authenticator; ✕ has none; – not observed.

columns.title: Last login
columns.header_tooltip: Duo's last successful login.

columns.title: User id
columns.header_tooltip: Duo's DU… id.

node.name: Outstanding bypass codes
node.description: Every bypass code a user holds right now: a passcode that satisfies MFA with no authenticator. ✕ under Expires? means Duo reported no expiration — the code never expires; a dash means the expiry was not observed.

columns.title: User
columns.header_tooltip: Who holds the code.

columns.title: User status
columns.header_tooltip: The holder's status.

columns.title: Expires?
columns.header_tooltip: ✓ the code expires (see the next column); ✕ Duo reported no expiration — it never expires; – not observed.

columns.title: Expires at
columns.header_tooltip: When the code expires, if it does.

columns.title: Uses left
columns.header_tooltip: Remaining uses as Duo reports it.

columns.title: Issued by
columns.header_tooltip: The administrator who created it, as Duo reports (email; not an identity link).

columns.title: Issued
columns.header_tooltip: When the code was created.

node.name: Administrators
node.description: Everyone who can change Duo, with their role and status. Whether each uses a phishing-resistant factor is counted in the posture strip.

columns.title: Administrator
columns.header_tooltip: The administrator's name.

columns.title: Email
columns.header_tooltip: Their Admin Panel login.

columns.title: Role
columns.header_tooltip: Owner, Administrator, Application Manager, User Manager, Security Analyst, Help Desk, Billing, Read-only, or a custom role.

columns.title: Status
columns.header_tooltip: Active, Disabled, Expired (blocked for inactivity), Pending Activation.

columns.title: Admin units
columns.header_tooltip: ✓ reach limited to administrative units; ✕ account-wide; – not observed.

columns.title: Last login
columns.header_tooltip: Last Admin Panel login.

node.name: Device health
node.description: The devices authentications come from and the posture Duo Desktop reports. A blank Duo Desktop version means the device is not reporting: its posture is unknown, not healthy.

columns.title: Device
columns.header_tooltip: Device name when Duo Desktop reports one.

columns.title: OS
columns.header_tooltip: Operating-system family.

columns.title: Version
columns.header_tooltip: Operating-system version.

columns.title: Trusted
columns.header_tooltip: ✓ a Trusted Endpoint (registered through a management integration); ✕ unmanaged; – not observed.

columns.title: Disk encryption
columns.header_tooltip: As Duo Desktop reports it.

columns.title: Firewall
columns.header_tooltip: As Duo Desktop reports it.

columns.title: Password
columns.header_tooltip: As Duo Desktop reports it.

columns.header_tooltip: The reporting Duo Desktop version; blank means no posture is reported.

entity.name: duo — account map: account, applications, policies, groups

node.name: duo — account map: account, applications, policies, groups
node.description: Scene search for the /duo account map: the selected account and the applications, policies and groups it holds (HOLDS_ACCOUNT_OBJECT__duo). The tenancy edges come with them and are hidden by the layout.

query: WHERE a.name STARTS_WITH $account AND a.name ENDS_WITH $account AND o.entity_type IN ["duo__duo_application", "duo__duo_policy", "duo__duo_group"]

account.description: The Duo account's name (duo__duo_account's natural key), from the page's ?account=. Empty — the default — selects every account, which is the single account on a grid that holds one. Matched as starts-with AND ends-with the value: Gryphon has no param-absent predicate (tap#360) and entity_id admits no string match, so this pair is the one predicate that is true of every account when the input is empty and selects the named account when it is not — together with any account whose name both starts and ends with it ("A" also selects "ABA"); the page's posture strip names such collisions. Exact-or-all arrives with tap#360.

node.name: duo account map layout
node.description: Hub layout (account-map.js, reusable by any page that mounts a Duo account scene): every account in the scene is a hub; its applications form a column on its left with the systems that request a second factor from them (and the services Duo SSO signs into) further out; the policies they enforce a column on its right; groups a row beneath; phones, hardware tokens and WebAuthn credentials folded into one tile per enrolled-device type above, each with its count. Tenancy edges are hidden (the hub is the tenancy); enforcement and group-access edges are drawn. Placement reads only entity types and edges, never ids, so it works for any account.
